description: HAVING clause with aggregate conditions: COUNT(*) > N, SUM >= threshold, groups that produce no match

steps.sql: CREATE TABLE orders (customer TEXT, amount INTEGER)
SELECT customer, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer HAVING COUNT(*) > 1 ORDER BY customer
steps.note: carol has only 1 order — filtered out by HAVING COUNT(*) > 1

steps.sql: SELECT customer, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer HAVING SUM(amount) >= 100 ORDER BY customer
steps.note: carol's total is 30 — filtered out by HAVING SUM >= 100

steps.sql: SELECT customer, COUNT(*) AS n FROM orders GROUP BY customer HAVING COUNT(*) > 5 ORDER BY customer
steps.note: No group has more than 5 orders — result is empty

steps.sql: SELECT customer, COUNT(*) AS n, SUM(amount) AS total FROM orders GROUP BY customer HAVING COUNT(*) >= 1 AND SUM(amount) > 50 ORDER BY customer
steps.note: Compound HAVING condition: carol excluded (total = 30, not > 50)
